proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences pair the terms indexed by \(k\) and \(p+k\) with opposite signs (while the intervening terms vanish), giving \(a(p+s)\equiv c(p+s)\equiv0\pmod p\) for \(0\le s<p\); at \(p-1=2m\), \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\) gives \(a(p-1)\equiv1\), while divisibility of the central binomial factors leaves only \(k=m\) in the \(c\)-sum, giving \(c(p-1)\equiv(-1)^m\). Hence both Hankel matrices are anti-triangular modulo \(p\); reversing the rows contributes sign \((-1)^m\), so their constant anti-diagonals yield determinants \((-1)^m\) and \(1\), respectively.
